explanation: Raytheon's first microwave ovens, sold in 1947, stood almost as tall as a person and went mainly to restaurants. Momofuku Ando launched instant noodles in Japan in 1958.

claims.text: Raytheon's first microwave ovens went on sale in 1947.
Momofuku Ando launched the first instant noodles, Chikin Ramen, in Japan in 1958.
The first microwave ovens stood almost as tall as a person and were sold mainly to restaurants and other businesses.

issues.note: checker_doubt c1: sources differ on when microwave ovens went on sale (Radarange 1947, the commercial 1161 model 1954, the first home oven 1955, a countertop home model 1967). The key holds for 1947, 1954 and 1955, but 1954 and 1955 are only three to four years before 1958, which would fail the 10-year guard (C17), and a player who counts home ovens would pick the noodles. Get dataset or web evidence for a first sale in 1947, or relabel (for example 'The first commercial microwave oven') and widen the gap.
